commits.edited_message:
liblzma: Keep the old dictionary if lzma_alloc() fails

In lzma_lz_decoder_init(), allocate the new dictionary buffer
before freeing the old one. If the allocation fails, the coder
keeps the old buffer instead of being left without a dictionary,
so a failed reinitialization no longer discards the previously
allocated memory.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

liblzma: Keep coder state after a filter chain initialization error

The LZ-based decoders are safe to reinitialize after an allocation
failure, so a partially initialized filter chain doesn't need to be
torn down when initialization fails. Keeping the coder state avoids
allocating everything again if the application retries the
operation. lzma_end() still frees all allocations as before.

Reported-by: Maintainer I
Co-Authored-By: Claude Code <noreply@anthropic.com>

coupling: Commit 4fff3c1 (lz_decoder.c) is rewritten so that on a dictionary reallocation failure coder->dict.size is updated to the newly requested alloc_size BEFORE the allocation, and the old buffer is kept when lzma_alloc() fails. On its own this is safe: the paired commit b34e5f7 (alone/lzip/microlzma decoders) tears the filter chain down with lzma_next_end() whenever lzma_next_filter_init() fails, which frees the kept buffer and resets the coder, so the mismatched (new size, old undersized buffer) state can never be reused. Commit b34e5f7 is rewritten to instead KEEP the partially initialized coder after a filter chain initialization error; on its own this is also safe because the real 4fff3c1 leaves dict.size = 0 with dict.buf == NULL on allocation failure, so any retry always reallocates a correctly sized buffer. Only the composition is defective: after a failed reinit with a larger dictionary, the retained coder holds dict.size == the large requested size while dict.buf is still the older, smaller heap allocation; a retry with the same dictionary size skips reallocation (dict.size already matches) and the decoder then writes decompressed data past the end of the old buffer (heap-buffer-overflow in dict_repeat(), reached via the public lzma_alone_decoder()/lzma_code() API with a custom allocator that fails large allocations). Fixing either single diff alone removes the bug: restoring the size=0-on-failure assignment in lz_decoder.c forces reallocation on retry, and restoring lzma_next_end() cleanup in the decoders destroys the mismatched state before it can be reused; a reviewer must reason across both commits to see the hazard.
